questions.stem: This plot shows a drug's plasma concentration over time after a single dose. Which elimination kinetics does it show?

explanation.summary: On a linear axis the concentration falls by the same amount (2.5 mg/mL) every 2 hours, giving a straight line. A constant amount removed per unit time, independent of concentration, is zero-order elimination (e.g., ethanol, high-dose phenytoin or aspirin).
explanation.whyCorrect: The concentration falls by the same amount (2.5 mg/mL) every 2 hours, giving a straight line on a linear axis. A constant amount removed per unit time is zero-order elimination.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Enterohepatic recirculation produces secondary peaks as drug is reabsorbed, not a steady linear decline.
whyWrongByChoice.B: First-order elimination removes a constant fraction per unit time, giving an exponential curve on a linear axis, not a straight line.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Flow-limited (high-extraction) elimination still follows first-order kinetics and declines exponentially.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Two-compartment kinetics gives a biphasic curve with a steep distribution phase and a slower elimination phase.

questions.stem: This plot shows a drug's plasma concentration over time after a single dose, on a linear y-axis. What does the shape of the curve indicate about the drug's elimination?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A constant absolute amount of drug is eliminated per unit time

choices.label: B
choices.text: A constant fraction of drug is eliminated per unit time

choices.label: C
choices.text: An increasing fraction is eliminated as concentration falls

choices.label: D
choices.text: Drug is eliminated only above a threshold concentration

choices.label: E
choices.text: Elimination stops once concentration reaches half the peak

explanation.summary: First-order kinetics removes a constant proportion of drug per unit time, so the elimination rate is proportional to concentration and the curve decays exponentially on a linear scale.
explanation.whyCorrect: First-order kinetics removes a constant proportion of drug per unit time, so the elimination rate is proportional to concentration and the curve decays exponentially on a linear scale.

whyWrongByChoice.A: A constant absolute amount per unit time defines zero-order kinetics, which gives a straight line on a linear plot.
whyWrongByChoice.C: An increasing fraction eliminated as concentration falls has no standard kinetic basis; first-order removes the same fraction at every concentration.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Threshold-dependent elimination is not a recognized kinetic order and would not produce smooth exponential decay.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Elimination continues past half the peak; each successive half-life removes another half of what remains.

questions.stem: A 22-year-old woman comes to the emergency department 12 hours after a single intentional ingestion of acetaminophen. Her serum acetaminophen level is 100 µg/mL. Based on this nomogram, what is the most appropriate next step?

choices.label: D
choices.text: Discharge; the level is below the treatment line

choices.label: E
choices.text: Repeat the level in 4 hours before treating

explanation.summary: On the Rumack-Matthew nomogram the treatment line starts at 150 µg/mL at 4 hours and halves about every 4 hours (about 37.5 µg/mL at 12 hours). A level of 100 µg/mL at 12 hours lies well above it, so N-acetylcysteine should be started now. The nomogram applies only to a single acute ingestion with a known time, from 4 hours onward.
explanation.whyCorrect: A level of 100 µg/mL at 12 hours plots well above the treatment line (about 37.5 µg/mL at 12 hours), so N-acetylcysteine is indicated to replenish glutathione and detoxify NAPQI.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Fomepizole inhibits alcohol dehydrogenase and treats methanol or ethylene glycol poisoning, not acetaminophen.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Naloxone reverses opioid toxicity and has no effect on acetaminophen hepatotoxicity.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The level plots above, not below, the treatment line at 12 hours.
whyWrongByChoice.E: A level above the line after 4 hours already indicates treatment; delaying N-acetylcysteine increases liver injury.
